# Halocarbon cross-section check (auto-generated by `build/halocarbon_check.py`)

Radiative efficiency (W m-2 ppb-1) computed from the HITRAN cross-sections versus AR6 Table 7.SM.7 (all-sky, stratosphere-adjusted).  Model: 1750 US-standard atmosphere with the MT_CKD water-vapour continuum, 10 ppt of the gas mixed uniformly, instantaneous top-of-atmosphere forcing.

* **clear sky** = no clouds;
* **all-sky estimate** = (1 - 0.67) x clear + 0.67 x grey cloud deck at 5-6 km, optical depth 0.68, tuned so the model longwave cloud effect is 27.9 W m-2 (CERES EBAF Ed4.0: 27.9).  The AR6 values play no part in this tuning, so the comparison is an independent test.

Clear-sky/AR6: 1.62-1.95 (mean 1.78).  All-sky estimate/AR6: 1.02-1.31 (mean 1.15, standard deviation 0.07).

Interpretation: the ratios cluster tightly, so no individual data set is missing a band.  The all-sky estimate removes most of the clear-sky excess; the residual reflects the simplicity of a one-deck cloud model, the single US-standard profile, the uniform vertical distribution of the halocarbons and the absence of stratospheric adjustment (which would raise our values).  Deck-height sensitivity: see `docs/cloud_sensitivity.md`.
